summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted for dyspnea, chest heaviness, and productive cough due to acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. He presented with weight gain, bibasilar crackles, and mild pulmonary edema on chest X-ray. He was treated with IV furosemide, resulting in improved symptoms and a weight reduction from 135.3 kg to 127.3 kg. His troponin elevation was attributed to heart strain and chronic kidney disease. He remained on home heart failure medications, with ranitidine switched to pantoprazole for GERD symptoms. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor daily weights, follow a low-salt diet, and complete outpatient labs and follow-up, including a repeat CT for a pulmonary nodule and a sleep study for suspected OSA.
